The Mishnah gives Dosa’s conditional New Year prayer.
The moon witness dispute explicitly names Dosa ben Horkenos and Yehoshua.
The passage gives Dosa’s view and Chanan. The second Mishnah continues Chanan’s rulings, while the next set is introduced as Admon’s.
Six consecutive Mishnayot give Dosa’s rulings. The first two and the fifth give the full patronym directly.
The named Mishnah gives Dosa’s threshold for the first shearing.
The opening ruling concerning components of corpse impurity also names Dosa ben Horkenos.
The named ruling gives thirty-six appearances of afflictions.
Maimonides places Dosa in Shimon the Righteous’s generation and explicitly says he reached Akiva’s generation. This passage does not calculate a lifespan of over four hundred years.
This local pointer repeats Dosa’s objection to the witnesses and the separate account of Yehoshua’s eventual compliance.
The pointer identifies the named local article. The Yevamot account expressly names all three visiting sages.
Yehoshua, Elazar ben Azaryah, and Akiva are named as visitors. Dosa seats Yehoshua and Elazar on gold couches and asks Akiva to sit.
The Bavli uses the testimony formula without expressly saying Dosa was an eyewitness. Heilprin offers transmission as an alternative.
Rabbi Dosa’s opinion is associated with the later generations in this argument.
The Mishnah gives Dosa’s ruling on the captive woman. The preceding unit supplies the full patronym.
Dosa expressly identifies his younger brother as Yonatan, a student of Shammai.
The Maharal explicitly considers both possibilities for Dosa’s parentage of Chanina.

The exact parallel at the end of Avot chapter 4 requires another witness. Maimonides’ independently checked introduction gives the specific chronology. The cited end of chapter 4 did not supply the parallel in the retrieved comment.

More than four hundred years is Heilprin’s calculation from the chronology he attributes to Maimonides. The introduction directly supplies the endpoints, while Heilprin subsequently rejects the inference. The figure is not explicit there.

The figure of two hundred years is conjectural and the token נ״ב remains unexpanded. Yevamot confirms the condition of Dosa’s eyes and his teaching about the mortar. It does not independently verify either number.
The exact G.A.Y. burial report remains uncollated. Preserve it as an attributed source notice; the research stage does not independently identify the cave.
The asserted Eliezer relationship remains open. The Bavli passage directly names younger brother Yonatan. Similar patronyms alone do not establish the distinct Eliezer claim.
The exact relevant passage within the named Tzadok pointer remains open. The direct evidence for Dosa’s chronology and for the possible parentage of Chanina is separate.
